items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: And people that were promoting that asked for Duke Ellington and Count Basie, I mean Duke Ellington, and the Cuttombs Band to play together.

ctx.x: I went to, what was it, my first time?

Oh, sure. I know we went up, went over to Europe. We went around near Belgium, went to England, and we went somewhere in Italy. Somewhere in Belgium was like a big place. You know, one place was behind the Iron Curtain, or something like that. But the woman that sang, was singing with Duke Ellington. She requested to sing Coastal Walk with us. And people that were promoting that asked for Duke Ellington and Count Basie, I mean Duke Ellington, and the Cuttombs Band to play together. And I was honored when Duke…
Then he had his fast song. He'd never miss it.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: I think he had a pitch of something like Jan Brushing that used to play with Count Basin, one of those kind of voices too.

ctx.x: What did Bud Scott do? I want to get this started.

Well I believe if he didn't play it he was a great singer. And he was one of those guys that could make up his own song, rhyme a song, and he had a good powerful voice. The band couldn't play any louder and he could sing. And the band was built around him, from what I understand. Was he a big guy, a little guy? I think he was a kind of big fellow. Big head, I think. I think he had, to me, he had a pitch of something like that. He had a pitch of something like Jan Brushing that used to play with Count Basin, one…
Could Clayborne Williams' band fake it all then?
